label: <DEL> step when the first original token is o (about to output o)
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (t == L), and in 99.9% of activation mass only when the first original token is o, i.e. the model is about to output o as the first copy token. It never fires in the original or copy phases. But it is very sparse inside that context: only about 4% of <DEL> steps with first token o activate. Longer sequences (L 6-8) are more likely to activate; L<=4 never does. Activation is more likely and stronger when the second token is 0 (precision 24%, and the top examples are o 0 ...), and when the prefix contains q/u/v, especially when the token right before <DEL> is u, v or e. None of these conditions separates active from inactive cases cleanly (best F1 about 0.25), so what makes it fire within the o-first context is still unexplained. It does not fire for other first tokens (only 4 such activations, first tokens 0/m/l).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=1 & out_tok=o (+4.28), out_tok=o (+3.61), orig2=s (+2.49), next_out=o (+2.12), prev_tok=u (+2.06), orig2=a (+1.97). Lower it: correct=1 (-4.93), orig5=- (-2.73), in_count=1 (-2.07), orig5=m (-1.92).
